free_tier.stated: Apache-2.0 software with no licence fee and no metered quota; the agents run on hardware the operator provides, so the cost is the host

per_object_cap.stated: no cap from the software; the agent host's memory and disk are the limit

interface_detail: a server plus one or more agents; a .woodpecker.yml pipeline; the woodpecker-cli
tooling: docker, podman, or a local backend on the agent host
chaining: pair it with a free VM and the per-job cap disappears, because the cap belongs to a hosted runner and not to the software

limits.value: no cap from the software; the agent host's memory and disk are the limit

identity_cost.detail: the software needs no account; the forge it authenticates against does

confidence_note: the project's own intro page and its repository licence were read, and Codeberg documents that it runs Woodpecker in production. The intro page does not state the licence, which is why the repository is cited separately.

evidence.proved: a server plus one or more agents, self-hosted, and 'lightweight and even runs on a Raspberry Pi'; the page names neither the licence nor a hosted instance
the project repository is licensed Apache-2.0, as GitHub's licence field for it reports
Codeberg's hosted instance is Woodpecker, and self-hosted agents can be attached to it

notes: This is the route that removes every per-job cap in this topic, and it is also the route that makes the cost a machine rather than a minute. Whether that is cheaper depends on the VM, which is the compute topic's question and not this one's.
